AgeOptions.description: holds the values for the `.age` section of the config file, the age alternative to the Ansible Vault password given by --vault-password-file.

identity_files.description:
are paths to identity files, each holding either the age private keys that
decrypt registry credentials or an SSH private key. A leading ~ is expanded to the home
directory of the user running cargoship. Equivalent to repeating --age-identity-file.

recipients.description:
are the public keys registry credentials are encrypted to, each either an age
recipient or an SSH public key. Equivalent to repeating --age-recipient.

recipients_files.description:
are paths to files holding public keys, one per line, with # comments
allowed, mixing age recipients and SSH public keys freely. An authorized_keys file works as
it is. A leading ~ is expanded to the home directory of the user running cargoship.
Equivalent to repeating --age-recipients-file.

DistroCreateOptions.description: holds the values for the `.distro.create` section of the config file

content_store.description:
is a local content bundle that images and files are resolved from instead
of being fetched over the network: a hauler store (https://github.com/hauler-dev/hauler)
as either a store directory or an archive written by `hauler store save`, or a built
zarf package (https://github.com/zarf-dev/zarf). Which format it is is read from the
bundle itself, not from the path. Content the store does not hold still comes from the
source the distro definition declared, so a partial store works. A file is accepted
from the store only when the definition declares a shasum for it, since nothing else
would verify bytes the definition's author never saw. Honoured by `cargoship create`.

Several bundles may be listed, and they are read as one: a zarf package carries a
single architecture by construction, so a build targeting two needs one package per
architecture. A file entry is answered by the first bundle holding that entry's
architecture, and an image reference by every bundle holding it at once.

file_override.description:
maps a source URL prefix to the location cargoship downloads from
instead, for example {"https://rpm.rancher.io": "https://mirror.example.com/rpm-rancher"}.
The value may also be a local directory, for builds from pre-staged assets.

hauler_store.description:
is the former spelling of ContentStore, which reads a hauler store and
nothing else.

Deprecated: set content_store instead, which reads the same hauler stores plus zarf
packages. This key is still honoured when content_store is unset.

registry_override.description:
maps a source registry to the registry cargoship uses instead
when pulling images, for example {"docker.io": "mirror.example.com"}

DistroOptions.description: holds the values for the `.distro` section of the config file

allow_downgrade.description:
whether a run continues when a host already runs an engine version newer
than the one the package carries

allow_unmanaged_nodes.description:
whether an apply continues when the cluster holds a node that no host
in the config accounts for

concurrency.description: how many nodes we will try to interact with at a time, 0 means that all nodes will be done at once

create.description: are options used by the create subcommand

firewall.description: whether we will update the host firewall

hosts.description: whether we will update the etc host file

kubeconfig.description:
path of the kubeconfig file the admin creds are merged into, the standard
location -- KUBECONFIG, else ~/.kube/config -- when empty

label_nodes.description: whether we will check and add the node-role.kubernetes.io/<profile> label on nodes

oci_concurrency.description: is how many concurrent oci artifacts that will be pushed at a time

output.description: the folder that we will create the distro tar balls in

public_key.description: path to public key file for validating signed packages

publish.description: are options used by the publish subcommand

receipt_path.description:
is where the lifecycle commands -- apply, prepare, reset and
engine-config-sync -- write the structured JSON record of a run, empty for no receipt.
Equivalent to --receipt-path, and templated the same way: {command} expands to the
command that ran and {timestamp} to when it started, so one configured value gives
every run its own file rather than overwriting the last.

retry.description:
how many times an operation is retried before the run fails, including a
package push to an OCI registry -- it is what --retries defaults to on publish
and sign

type.description: of distro we are interacting with

update_kubeconfig.description: whether we will update a kubeconfig file with the admin creds for the cluster

worker_concurrency.description:
number of worker nodes that will be upgraded at once, as a fixed count
("5") or a percentage of the batch ("25%")

DistroPublishOptions.description: holds the values for the `.distro.publish` section of the config file

signing_key.description: is the private key used to sign, or re-sign, the package: a local file path, or env://ENV_VAR to read the key from an environment variable. Cloud KMS references are not supported -- they cannot be reached from an air-gapped management node.

signing_key_password.description: the password for the private key used for signing

FileOverrideMap.description: maps a source URL prefix to the location cargoship downloads from instead.

RegistryOverrideMap.description: maps a source registry to the registry cargoship uses instead.

description: holds the values for the `.`, or root, section of the config file

age.description: are the age keys used to encrypt and decrypt registry credentials

architecture.description: the CPU architecture to use for OCI operations

distro.description: are various options used by the command

log_file.description: enables always writing a full-verbosity debug log to a file, regardless of LogLevel

log_format.description: how the logs are displayed well running

log_level.description: the level of logs that will be displayed

no_color.description: whether to disable terminal color codes in logging and stdout prints

timeout.description: the longest we will run long ran tasks before failing

tmp_dir.description: the directory where we store stuff before deleting them

zarf_cache.description: is the folder where cargoship caches what it fetches: oras artifacts, and the release assets the example generation targets read
